experiment: Kalshi market making: v1 against the v2 engine
headline: Collecting: day 0 of 14 before the arms are scored against each other. Running totals, not results: baseline -0.37 over 15 fills; v2_niche +1.88 over 52 fills; v2_crypto +0.42 over 169 fills.

arms.name: baseline
arms.description: v1 unchanged: Avellaneda-Stoikov quotes around the touch mid on niche markets, crossing the spread to flatten before game windows and closes.

arms.name: v2_niche
arms.description: v2 engine on the same universe: edge curve around a depth-weighted mid, never crosses, reduce-only instead of flatten, holds to resolution.

arms.name: v2_crypto
arms.description: v2 engine on hourly BTC/ETH strike ladders, fair value from Binance anchored to the Kalshi book, exposure netted across strikes.

kill_criteria: A treatment whose realized expectancy per resolved contract is negative after 200 contracts is stopped.
Any aggregate exposure breach, or a position held into a resolution rule nobody read, stops that arm until fixed.
Written before the first v2 paper fill (2026-09-25); not moved after seeing results.
caveats: Paper fills. v2's venue is stricter than v1's: v2 queues behind the size at its own price and waits 0.5s for acks and cancels; v1 queues behind the top of book and fills instantly. That bias works against v2.
v1 marks open inventory at the last mid it saw; v2 holds to resolution and settles at 0 or 100.
Days lost to the laptop sleeping are lost for every arm at once.
